# Finding ∫ x³·sin(x) dx

I'll use **integration by parts** repeatedly (tabular method).

## Setting up the Tabular Method

| Sign | Differentiate (u) | Integrate (dv) |
|------|-------------------|----------------|
| +    | x**3             | sin(x)         |
| −    | 3*x**2           | −cos(x)        |
| +    | 6*x              | −sin(x)        |
| −    | 6                | cos(x)         |
| +    | 0                | sin(x)         |

## Combining (diagonal products with alternating signs)

$$\int x^3 \sin(x)\,dx = x^3(-\cos x) - 3x^2(-\sin x) + 6x(\cos x) - 6(\sin x) + C$$

## Simplifying

$$= -x^3\cos(x) + 3x^2\sin(x) + 6x\cos(x) - 6\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification (differentiating)

- d/dx[−x³·cos(x)] = −3x²·cos(x) + x³·sin(x)
- d/dx[3x²·sin(x)] = 6x·sin(x) + 3x²·cos(x)
- d/dx[6x·cos(x)] = 6·cos(x) − 6x·sin(x)
- d/dx[−6·sin(x)] = −6·cos(x)

Sum: x³·sin(x) + (6x·sin(x) − 6x·sin(x)) + (−3x²·cos(x) + 3x²·cos(x)) + (6·cos(x) − 6·cos(x)) = **x³·sin(x)** ✓

<answer>-x**3*cos(x) + 3*x**2*sin(x) + 6*x*cos(x) - 6*sin(x) + C</answer>

= x^3*sin(x) + (6x*sin(x) - 6x*sin(x)) + (-3x^2*cos(x) + 3x^2*cos(x)) + (6*cos(x) - 6*cos(x))
